newsitem.title: ALBANIA: New election row greets Vranitzky in Albania.
newsitem.headline: New election row greets Vranitzky in Albania.

text.p: European envoy to Albania Franz Vranitzky, trying to keep the country's disputed election process on track, on Sunday ran into a fresh row with smaller opposition parties protesting at how the vote will be held.

Leaders of the smaller parties gathered at Prime Minister Bashkim Fino's office, hoping to meet the former Austrian Chancellor and persuade him to hammer out a compromise in the dispute, which arose late on Saturday.

Vranitzky is heading an effort by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to assist Albania's early elections after months of unrest and chaos triggered by the collapse of fraudulent savings schemes early this year.

About eight of Albania's over 20 main parties said they would reconsider whether to run in the June 29 parliamentary vote. They were protesting at changes made on Saturday to plans for the distribution of some seats.

"There is no point going to the elections with this change," Fatmir Mehdiu, a senior leader of the Republican party, told Reuters. His party is one of nine in Fino's interim government, formed in March to guide the country to elections.
The country's constitutional court on Saturday overturned a previously agreed plan to give a quota of some of the 155 parliamentary seats to smaller parties.

Of the total, 115 are to be chosen by simple majority voting and 40 by proportional representation; the court rejected as unconstitutional a plan to allocate the lion's share of these to smaller parties.
Mehdiu said the smaller parties also wanted to voice concerns at delays in getting their candidates approved as eligible for election.
Vranitzky was originally due to meet local OSCE officials and hold talks with President Sali Berisha, Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and leaders of the two main political parties.
Tension has been mounting as polling day approaches. A brief burst of gunfire rang out in the streets near the OSCE's headquarters a few minutes after Vranitzky went in.
